title: A Garden for the Thorn
premise: Lior Iversen has spent her life making herself small: a beast-speaker in a kingdom that burns such gifts, hiding behind the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things for those who can pay. When the border wards collapse and every star vanishes in a single night, Lior traces both catastrophes to the crown itself—a parasitic entity called the Regent that has been slowly devouring King Aldric and feeding on the kingdom's magic. To reach the truth she must ally with a disgraced warden, a traitorous guildmaster, and the king's own estranged daughter, while her gift—once her deepest shame—becomes the only key to unbinding him. In the end, Lior learns that justice outside the law demands a price: she must let the Regent wear her instead, long enough to be cast out, and choose who she is when she is no longer invisible.
about_author: Wren Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing rare manuscripts before turning to fiction full-time. They write fantasy about quiet people forced into loud histories, and live somewhere rainy with an opinionated dog.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. We meet her in the Vellum Guild's counting house, balancing accounts of impossible trades—a bottled storm, a year of someone else's luck—while secretly listening to the rats gossip beneath the floorboards. She refuses a dangerous commission from a hooded client. Emotional beat: the comfort of invisibility, and its first hairline crack.

chapters.title: What the Rats Saw
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The guild's messenger animals bring word of strange silences along the border: birds gone mute, wards humming wrong. Lior dismisses it until a dying fox staggers into the city and speaks her name. Emotional beat: dread creeping past the ledger lines; her gift is a liability she can no longer ignore.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At midnight every star goes out, and the border wards fall with them like snapped harp strings. The city erupts in panic; the Guild locks its doors and begins hoarding. Lior realizes the fox's warning and the darkness arrived together. Emotional beat: terror and a terrible exhilaration—the world just made hiding impossible.

chapters.title: A Commission in Ash
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The hooded client returns, revealed as Sera Vane, a disgraced royal warden hunting whoever dropped the wards. She offers Lior immunity for her gift in exchange for help reading the Guild's sealed ledgers. Emotional beat: wary bargain; two women who trust no one deciding to trust each other slightly.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Smile
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane's POV. Corvane knows what Lior is—and always has. He reveals the Guild sold the ward-lattice to an anonymous buyer years ago, and he intends to profit from the chaos rather than fix it. He offers Lior partnership in silence. Emotional beat: betrayal; the shelter was also a cage, and the jailer wants a business partner.

chapters.title: Ledgers Written in Blood-Price
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Decoding the sealed ledgers with Sera, Lior finds payments routed to the palace itself—enormous sums buying 'maintenance of the crown.' The trail leads to King Aldric, beloved and reclusive for a decade. Emotional beat: dawning horror that the rot sits at the very top.

chapters.title: The Princess Who Ran
chapters.summary: Princess Isolde's POV. Introduce Isolde, exiled to a border convent after publicly accusing her father of 'not being her father.' She has spent ten years collecting proof. Sera brings her Lior's findings. Emotional beat: vindication curdling with grief; being right cost her everything.

chapters.title: Beasts at the Broken Border
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The trio travels to the fallen wards. Lior speaks with the wild animals there and learns the truth: something crossed the border long ago, wearing the king like a coat, and it drank the stars to stay fed. Emotional beat: awe and fear as her shameful gift becomes the story's compass.

chapters.title: Corvane's Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane's POV. Corvane sells their route to the palace guard, believing a controlled crisis will make the Guild indispensable to whatever wears the crown next. His chapter reveals his philosophy: power is simply a ledger with better margins. Emotional beat: cold ambition; the corruption theme given a human face.

chapters.title: Into the Silent Palace
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Smuggled in as Guild auditors, they enter a palace where servants move like sleepwalkers and no one meets anyone's eyes. Lior hears, through the mice in the walls, a second heartbeat under the throne room. Emotional beat: claustrophobic dread; the court is already half-devoured.

chapters.title: The Audience
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde faces her father for the first time in ten years. For one breath, Aldric surfaces—begging her, in a child's cipher they invented, to run. Then the Regent looks out through his eyes and greets her by name. Emotional beat: heartbreak; the father is still in there, drowning.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera recognizes the Regent from old warden records: a bound spirit meant to advise kings, unbound by greed, now consuming host and kingdom alike. It offers each of them their heart's desire if they walk away. Sera nearly takes it. Emotional beat: temptation; power corrupts by offering exactly what you already want.

chapters.title: The Price of Knowing
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The Regent identifies Lior's gift and reveals why beast-speakers are burned: their voices can unmake bindings—including its own. It orders her death, but Corvane's guards arrive first, arresting all three on fabricated treason charges. Emotional beat: despair; knowing the answer makes her the target.

chapters.title: Cells and Cages
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Imprisoned beneath the palace, the trio plans through the walls—literally, as Lior relays messages via rats. Isolde confronts her guilt over abandoning her father, and chooses to stop running. Emotional beat: resolve forged in a cell; identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Ledger
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane's POV. Corvane comes to gloat and negotiate, but Lior shows him the final page of his own future: the Regent's ledgers list him as an expense to be settled once the stars are fully consumed. For the first time, Corvane's arithmetic fails him. Emotional beat: the schemer realizing he is merchandise.

chapters.title: Escape by Tooth and Claw
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. With Corvane's reluctant aid and an army of city beasts, they break out during a blackout the Regent causes to feed. Lior speaks to a thousand creatures at once for the first time and nearly loses herself in their minds. Emotional beat: power surging toward corruption's edge; her gift could devour her too.

chapters.title: The Binding Rite
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. In the ruined ward-tower, Sera reconstructs the original binding rite—but it requires a voice the Regent cannot refuse to hear, spoken from inside its circle. Everyone understands what that means. Lior volunteers before anyone else can. Emotional beat: sacrifice accepted without melodrama; justice chosen over safety.

chapters.title: Throne of Hunger
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. They storm the throne room as the last starlight fails. The Regent unleashes the hollowed court against them; Sera falls defending Isolde, gravely wounded but alive. Lior walks the killing floor untouched because the beasts will not obey the Regent anymore. Emotional beat: climax ignites; courage amid ruin.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Inside the circle, Lior lets the Regent take her—as it took the king—so she can speak the unbinding from within its own throat. She experiences its endless hunger and nearly becomes it, saved by the sound of Isolde speaking her true name. The binding shatters; the Regent unravels screaming into the dark. Emotional beat: the climax's peak—identity as the weapon that defeats consumption.

chapters.title: The King in the Ruin
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Aldric wakes, ten years stolen, old and diminished and himself. His reunion with Isolde is not forgiveness but beginning. He abdicates rather than rule a kingdom that watched him be eaten, naming Isolde regent. Emotional beat: bittersweet restoration; some things are recovered, not repaired.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The new regency wants to honor Lior; the old law still wants to burn her gift. She refuses both, testifying publicly about the Guild's complicity and forcing Corvane to surrender his ledgers to open audit. Justice arrives not from the crown but from testimony. Emotional beat: hard-won integrity; the law remade by truth rather than throne.

chapters.title: A Garden for the Thorn
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Months later, Lior plants a garden where the ward-tower fell, teaching other hidden gifted children that their voices are not curses. A thorned rose grows over the old binding-stone—beautiful and sharp, like everything she's learned. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; she is visible now, and it does not destroy her.
